note: Sus4 heard against the plain chord (sus:1) on the chord circle: C and Csus4 tapped in turn until the 4th is heard falling to the 3rd, then G and Gsus4, the second key, with the fall heard ahead and a line on what stays the same. Chord tokens have no sus chords, so the chord names stay letters, the keys are fixed and there are no moves.

exercise.title: Sus4: the 4th in place of the 3rd
exercise.why: A sus4 chord swaps the 3rd for the 4th, the next note up the scale, so it is neither major nor minor until the 4th falls back to the 3rd.

cells.text:
The chord circle below has the C chord in the middle and, around it, the chords it can turn into. Tap the middle to hear C. Then tap Csus4: it has {{4}} in place of {{3}}.
Go from Csus4 back to C. Practice until you hear {{4}} falling to {{3}} each time.

The chord circle below has the G chord in the middle. Tap the middle, then Gsus4, then the middle again.
Then tap Gsus4 and wait: hear in your head the note it will fall to, then tap the middle to check.
In G the notes are new, and the sus4 chord still has {{4}} standing in for {{3}} and falling back to it.
